title: Applied Materials (AMAT) Stock Sinks As Market Gains: What You Should Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: Applied Materials (AMAT) declined 1.97% to $404.98, underperforming the broader market which gained 0.28%. The stock has lost 11.01% prior to today's trading. However, the company is expected to report strong earnings on November 12, 2026, with projected EPS of $4.06 (up 87.10% YoY) and revenue of $10.3 billion (up 51.4% YoY). AMAT currently holds a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) with a Forward P/E of 32.3 and PEG ratio of 1.15.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While AMAT experienced a near-term decline and underperformed the market, strong forward-looking fundamentals support a neutral stance. Expected earnings growth of 87.10% YoY and revenue growth of 51.4% YoY are positive, but the stock's recent 11.01% loss and Hold rating (Zacks Rank #3) indicate near-term weakness. The valuation metrics (Forward P/E 32.3, PEG 1.15) are in line with industry averages, suggesting fair pricing without significant upside or downside catalysts in the immediate term.

title: Applied Materials vs. Broadcom: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Erin Kennedy
description: The article compares two AI infrastructure leaders: Applied Materials, which manufactures semiconductor equipment with steady 4.4% revenue growth and a 24.7% net margin, and Broadcom, which designs specialized chips and software with impressive 23.9% revenue growth and 36.2% net margin. While Broadcom has outperformed significantly over the past decade, the author favors Applied Materials for 2026, citing its more reasonable valuation and greater growth potential given Broadcom's larger market cap and proximity to a growth ceiling.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Author prefers this stock for 2026 due to reasonable valuation (P/E 38.51), steady financial performance with 24.7% net margin, strong free cash flow of $5.7B, and greater room for growth compared to Broadcom. The author notes it has outpaced the S&P 500 over 10 years despite modest current growth.

While Broadcom shows impressive financial metrics (36.2% net margin, $26.9B free cash flow, 23.9% revenue growth) and major customer agreements, the author considers it expensive relative to future prospects. High debt ($67.12B), regulatory scrutiny, and elevated valuation (P/E 44.20) suggest limited upside, with the company approaching a growth ceiling due to its large market cap.
Mentioned as a deep partnership with Applied Materials on next-generation manufacturing, but no independent assessment provided in the article.
Referenced as a major customer of Broadcom with a $30 billion chip commitment, but no independent sentiment assessment provided.

title: Intel vs. Qualcomm: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Erin Kennedy
description: Intel is undergoing a massive foundry business transformation to compete in AI chip manufacturing, but faces significant losses, negative free cash flow, and suspended dividends. Qualcomm maintains strong profitability with 12.5% net margins and robust free cash flow of $12.8 billion, while expanding in 5G, automotive, and computing markets. Despite Intel's higher 5-year performance, the author recommends Qualcomm as the better buy due to superior financial metrics and lower valuation, though suggests an S&P 500 ETF as the optimal choice.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company reported $267 million net loss in fiscal 2025, negative free cash flow of $4.9 billion, suspended dividend, and is in midst of costly business overhaul. Unfavorable valuation with forward P/E of 63.7 and P/S ratio of 9.2. Faces intense competition and requires significant capital expenditures.

Strong financial performance with $5.5 billion net income, 12.5% net margin, and robust free cash flow of $12.8 billion. Revenue growth of 13.7% year-over-year. More attractive valuation with forward P/E of 17.1 and P/S ratio of 4.1. Pays modest 2.1% dividend yield.
Mentioned as Intel's partnership deepening for foundry business expansion. No direct financial analysis provided; appears as supporting player in Intel's strategy.
Mentioned as major customer of Qualcomm, representing customer concentration risk. No independent analysis provided.

Author's preferred investment choice over both individual stocks, noting that neither Intel nor Qualcomm matched S&P 500 returns over 10 years, making the broad index fund a better option for outperforming individual semiconductor stocks.

title: ASML vs. Applied Materials: Which Chip-Equipment Stock Is the Better Buy?
author: Adam Levy
description: With semiconductor manufacturers expanding production capacity to meet AI chip demand, both ASML and Applied Materials are positioned for strong growth. ASML dominates lithography equipment with ~90% market share and premium pricing power, while Applied Materials offers a diversified portfolio with opportunities to gain market share through integrated solutions. Despite similar forward P/E ratios around 40x, Applied Materials appears the better long-term buy, trading at 21x 2028 earnings versus ASML's 23x, given its potential for sustained higher growth rates post-investment cycle.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy with a broad, diversified equipment portfolio, strong R&D capabilities, and significant opportunity to expand market share through integrated solutions and cross-selling. Long-term growth potential is highlighted as superior to ASML, with more attractive 2028 valuation metrics.

Recognized as an absolutely dominant force with ~90% lithography market share, years ahead of competitors, and premium pricing power. Strong near-term earnings growth expected from capacity expansion and higher-margin equipment sales, though limited room for market share gains constrains long-term upside.
Mentioned as a beneficiary of the semiconductor expansion cycle with continuously rising capital expenditure budgets, but not directly compared or analyzed in the investment recommendation.
